app.name: Shopify (Partner Dashboard / Dev Dashboard app with Admin API OAuth)

verdict.summary: Using your own Shopify app on your own development store or a single store needs no Shopify review, but Composio gives you no managed app, so you must create and maintain your own app credentials. Public distribution (installable on many stores) needs Shopify approval and an App Store listing, and protected customer data adds further gates.
verdict.hands_on_effort: About 1-2 hours for a private or development-store setup. Public distribution is several days of listing and compliance work plus the review wait.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Same day once a development store exists (estimate, not from sources).
verdict.approval_wait: None for custom distribution or development stores. Public App Store review has no official turnaround; community reports run about 1-2 weeks per cycle, with anecdotes up to about a month.

gates.name: Development store / custom distribution (works for you)
gates.unlocks: Create your own Shopify app, install it on your own development store, and connect your own account through Composio.
limits: Custom distribution is limited to a single store, stores in one Plus organization, or development stores.
Custom distribution cannot charge merchants through Shopify's app billing system.
The distribution method cannot be changed after you select it.
Admin-created custom apps can no longer be made for new apps since January 1, 2026; new apps are built in the Dev Dashboard.

gates.name: Custom distribution to specific stores (invited/test users, no review)
gates.unlocks: Install the app on named stores (one store, stores in one Plus organization, or development stores) and request protected customer data scopes for development use.
limits: Apps installed only on development stores can read protected customer data after scopes are selected in the Partner Dashboard, without review.
Protected customer data access requires a distribution method to be selected first, even for development stores.
Protected customer data is off by default. The API does not return data from non-development stores until the app is approved for it (for public apps).
Online access tokens last while the app is installed or 24 hours, whichever is first.
Offline access tokens last as long as the app is installed. A 60-minute expiry for new offline tokens is reported by a third party and is unverified.
gates.time_to_reach: Hours after Gate 1, depending on protected-data paperwork.

gates.name: Public distribution / App Store listing (works for anyone)
gates.unlocks: Install on any merchant's store through a public listing, including a listing set to unlisted visibility.
limits: Public distribution requires Shopify approval and an App Store listing, with a one-time fee.
Unlisted public apps are still reviewed according to community reports (not confirmed on an official page).
Level 2 protected customer data (name, address, phone, email) requires review for public apps and a data protection review may follow.
Apps using APIs deprecated within 90 days cannot be submitted.
Review status moves through Draft, Submitted, Reviewed, Published, and can enter Paused when core requirements fail.
gates.time_to_reach: Several days of listing and compliance work plus review. Community reports about 1-2 weeks per review cycle; possible Paused loops add time.

steps.title: Confirm you need your own app credentials
steps.detail: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Shopify, so you must register your own Shopify app and use its client ID and client secret in Composio. Decide now whether the app will be custom (one store, a Plus organization, or development stores) or public, because the distribution method cannot be changed after you select it.
gotchas: Do not start with a legacy admin-created custom app. Shopify closed that route for new apps on January 1, 2026.
Pick the distribution method on your production app if you run separate dev and prod apps.

steps.title: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard
steps.detail: Open the Partner Dashboard at partners.shopify.com/current/apps and create a new app in the Dev Dashboard. Enter the app name, app URL, and redirection URLs. Shopify's custom-app flow uses this same app setup.
gotchas: The exact field labels in the current Dev Dashboard were not verified. Check the screen directly.

steps.title: Add the Composio callback URL as an allowed redirection URL
steps.detail: Copy the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config and add it to the app's allowed redirection URLs. The install redirect must match this URL exactly, character for character.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: A trailing slash or a different host causes a mismatch at install time.
Composio's default redirect is a template. The callback URL in your auth config is the one that counts.

steps.title: Narrow the scope list to what your app needs
steps.detail: Draft a short list of the scopes your agent actually needs, each with a one-line justification. Remove the scopes Composio includes by default, which are not a Shopify requirement. Flag any scope that needs Shopify approval or touches protected customer data.

values.label: Example minimum
values.value: read_products, read_orders (add write_* only where needed)

gotchas: Any scope that writes a resource also grants read on it.
Add read_all_orders only if you need orders older than the default window, and only with read_orders or write_orders.

steps.title: Declare the scopes and deploy the app config
steps.detail: Declare the narrowed scopes in the app configuration (the access_scopes section of the app TOML) and deploy the app. Merchants approve the scopes on the OAuth grant page when they install.
gotchas: Scopes marked 'Shopify approval required' cannot be declared until Shopify approves them. Contact Shopify Support to request them.

steps.title: Create a development store and generate an install link
steps.detail: Create a development store in the Partner Dashboard. In the app's settings, click Generate link, enter the store's myshopify.com domain, and open the installation link to install the app on that store.

steps.title: Enter client ID and secret in Composio and connect your account
steps.detail: In Composio, create a Shopify auth config that uses your own app's client ID and client secret. Confirm the Composio callback URL matches what you added in Shopify, then connect your account to the development store. The authorize URL is per store, so you will enter the store subdomain when connecting.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Verify hmac, state or nonce, and that the shop value ends in myshopify.com. Composio handles this in its flow, but a custom integration must check all three.
Apps must run OAuth first, before any other install step.

steps.title: Test the authorization and token lifetime
steps.detail: Run a test authorization against the development store and record the token type and expiry. Online tokens last until uninstall or 24 hours, whichever comes first, so plan for refresh. Check the offline token lifetime against Shopify's own docs before relying on the reported 60-minute expiry.
gotchas: The 60-minute offline token expiry comes from a third-party blog, not from a Shopify page.

steps.title: Request protected customer data access if your agent needs it
steps.detail: In the Partner Dashboard, open Apps, select your app, go to API access requests, and click Request access for Protected customer data. Give reasons for each data field (name, address, email, phone) and complete the Data protection details. Development-store access works after the scopes are selected, with no review.
gotchas: Without approval, the API does not return protected customer data from non-development stores.
Select a distribution method before you start this request.

steps.title: Implement the mandatory compliance webhooks
steps.detail: Implement the three mandatory compliance webhooks before submitting for public review. Community reports say these are required even for unlisted apps. Draft the privacy policy text the listing will need.
gotchas: The webhook list is from a third-party source. Confirm it against Shopify's current app requirements.

steps.title: Prepare the App Store listing content
steps.detail: Prepare the listing: privacy policy URL, support and listing content, 3-6 desktop screenshots at 1600x900, a feature media item, a demo development store link, an app name of 30 characters or fewer, and a 100-character introduction. Record a complete screencast of setup and functionality, with clear test instructions and valid test credentials if you connect to a third-party platform.
gotchas: The app must perform OAuth immediately before any other install step, and must not use pop-ups for OAuth.
Some reviewers have flagged install flows that start at the app's own login page.

steps.title: Run the self-assessment review checklist
steps.detail: Open Apps, select your app, then go to Distribution, App Store, and Review requirements. Work through the checklist covering API scopes, GDPR webhooks, billing, design, and listing completeness.
gotchas: The checklist location comes from a third-party guide. Confirm it on your Partner Dashboard.

steps.title: Submit the app for review
steps.detail: Submit the app for Shopify App Store review from the distribution screen. Track its status: Draft, Submitted, Reviewed, Published. If it is Paused, fix the listed issues and resubmit.

steps.title: Wait for review and respond to requests
steps.detail: Shopify does not publish a fixed review turnaround. Community reports say about 1-2 weeks per cycle, with possible additional time for a data protection review or a Paused loop. Watch the Partner Dashboard and answer any Shopify requests quickly.
gotchas: Third-party sources conflict. Plan for at least two weeks, and longer if a data protection review is triggered.

requirements.item: Your own Shopify app with client ID and secret
requirements.detail: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Shopify, so you must register your own app and add its credentials to Composio.
Choose custom or public distribution before any protected-data request. The choice cannot be changed later.
The Composio callback URL must be in the app's allowed redirection URLs, matching the install redirect exactly.

requirements.item: Dev Dashboard app for new custom apps
requirements.detail: New custom apps are built in the Dev Dashboard and installed on the store. The admin-created custom app route closed January 1, 2026.
Declare the scopes and request protected-data access in the Partner Dashboard. Development-store access works without review; non-development store access needs approval.
Implement three compliance webhooks before public review. Community reports say these are required even for unlisted apps.
A privacy policy is required for public listing, along with support content, screenshots, a demo store link, and an app introduction.

requirements.item: OAuth first in the install flow
requirements.detail: OAuth must run immediately before any other install step. No pop-ups. Do not begin installs at a separate app login page.
Apps using APIs deprecated within 90 days cannot be submitted.
Provide a complete screencast of setup and functionality, clear test instructions, and valid test credentials for third-party platforms.
A third-party blog reports that public apps using non-expiring offline tokens must migrate by January 1, 2027. Verify on shopify.dev. Today is 2026-10-28, so this is close.

scopes.effect: Standard scopes. No special approval reported. Write scopes also grant read.
Standard order access, limited to the default 60-day window. Declare read_all_orders to reach older orders.
Shopify approval required before you can declare it. Does not grant access on its own; declare it alongside read_orders or write_orders.
Customer data may be protected customer data. Non-development stores need approval before data is returned.
Shopify approval required. Shopify must approve your app for each scope before you can declare it.

scopes.scope: Other labelled scopes (for example read_script_tags, write_themes)
scopes.effect: Some labelled scopes require contacting Shopify Support and explaining the need. Check the access scopes page for each scope before declaring it.

blockers.symptom: You cannot create a new custom app from the Shopify admin.
blockers.cause: Shopify closed admin-created custom apps for new apps on January 1, 2026.
blockers.fix: Build the app in the Dev Dashboard, then install it on your store with a generated installation link.

blockers.symptom: Public distribution is blocked pending approval, or the app cannot be installed on other stores.
blockers.cause: Public distribution requires Shopify approval and an App Store listing. Unreviewed public apps cannot be installed on production stores.
blockers.fix: Use custom distribution for single-store or Plus-organization installs, or go through the public App Store review.

blockers.symptom: The API returns no customer name, address, email, or phone data from a live store.
blockers.cause: Protected customer data is off by default and is not returned from non-development stores until the app is approved for it.
blockers.fix: Declare the scopes, request protected-data access in the Partner Dashboard, and complete the Data protection details. Plan for a data protection review on Level 2 fields.
blockers.contact: Partner Dashboard > Apps > [your app] > API access requests

blockers.symptom: A scope cannot be declared in the app config.
blockers.cause: Some scopes are labelled 'Shopify approval required'.
blockers.fix: Contact Shopify Support, explain why the app needs the scope, and wait for approval before declaring it.

blockers.symptom: Install fails at the redirect step.
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri does not exactly match an allowed redirection URL in the app.
blockers.fix: Copy the Composio callback URL from your auth config into the app's allowed redirection URLs exactly.

blockers.symptom: App is Paused or rejected during review.
blockers.cause: Core requirements failed, such as missing compliance webhooks, OAuth not first in the install flow, or deprecated APIs.
blockers.fix: Fix the listed requirements, then resubmit. Check the self-assessment checklist before submitting.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Shopify, so you must create your own Shopify app and use its client ID and secret. Composio uses a per-store myshopify.com authorize and token URL and its own default redirect URI, which must be in your app's allowed redirection URLs. The default scope list is Composio's own and is not a Shopify requirement; narrow it to what your app needs, because several scopes touch protected customer data or require Shopify approval.

evidence.claim: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Shopify, so the developer must bring their own Shopify app credentials.
evidence.quote: "managed_oauth_available": false

evidence.claim: You must select a distribution method before you can request protected customer data access, even for development stores.
evidence.quote: Before you can request access to protected customer data, including on development stores, you need to select a distribution method for your app.

evidence.claim: Apps installed only on development stores can read protected customer data after the scopes are selected in the Partner Dashboard, without submitting for review.
evidence.quote: If your app is for testing or installed only on a development store, you can access customer data in development after Step 5.

evidence.claim: Protected customer data is split into Level 1 (customer data without name, address, phone, email) and Level 2 (including those fields). For public apps both levels require review; for custom apps both are always available.
evidence.quote: | 2 | Requires review | Always available | Varies by plan

evidence.claim: Level 2 requires meeting all Level 1 and Level 2 requirements, including encrypted backups, separated test and production data, staff access limits, access logs, and an incident response policy; Shopify may run a data protection review, likely for apps with many installs or customer records.
evidence.quote: Data protection reviews will likely focus on apps that have

evidence.claim: Some access scopes are labelled 'Shopify approval required' (for example read_all_orders, read_customer_payment_methods, read_checkout_settings, read_shopify_payments, read_marketplace_orders); for other labelled scopes you contact Shopify Support and explain why the app needs them.
evidence.quote: Shopify has to approve your app for the scope before you can declare it.

evidence.claim: read_all_orders extends access beyond the default 60-day order window and must be declared alongside read_orders or write_orders; it does not grant access by itself.
evidence.quote: Doesn't grant access on its own. Declare it alongside read_orders or write_orders to extend that scope to older orders.

evidence.claim: Shopify restricts scope access for apps without a legitimate use for the data, and any scope that writes a resource also grants read on it, so requesting only what you need is expected.
evidence.quote: Shopify restricts access to scopes for apps that don't have a legitimate use for the associated data.

evidence.claim: Scopes for a new app are declared in the app config (TOML access_scopes section); merchants approve them on the OAuth grant page at install.
evidence.quote: For a new app, declare the scopes it needs and deploy your app. Merchants approve the scopes when they install it.

evidence.claim: Redirect URLs: the redirect_uri must be added to the app as an allowed redirection URL in the Partner Dashboard, and the install redirect must match it exactly.
evidence.quote: The complete URL specified here must be added to your app as an allowed redirection URL, as defined in the Partner Dashboard.

evidence.claim: Authorization code flow: the developer redirects the merchant to /admin/oauth/authorize with client_id, scope, redirect_uri, and a nonce; then exchanges the code at /admin/oauth/access_token with client_id and client_secret, after verifying hmac, state/nonce, and that shop ends with myshopify.com.
evidence.quote: The shop parameter is a valid shop hostname, ends with myshopify.com

evidence.claim: Authorization URL template is per store: https://{subdomain}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/authorize; token URL is the same host at /admin/oauth/access_token.
evidence.quote: "authorization_url": "https://{{subdomain}}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/authorize"

evidence.claim: Embedded apps are told to use token exchange rather than the manual authorization code grant; all apps are told to use Shopify managed installation; the manual grant guide is for non-embedded and legacy apps.
evidence.quote: Embedded apps should use token exchange to acquire access tokens, and all apps should use Shopify managed installation.

evidence.claim: Access tokens: online tokens are valid while the app is installed or for 24 hours, whichever is first, and then must be refreshed; offline tokens last as long as the app is installed.
evidence.quote: An online access token can be used for as long as the app is installed or for the next 24 hours, whichever comes first.

evidence.claim: A reported 2026 change: new offline access tokens expire after 60 minutes and come with a refresh token; public apps using non-expiring offline tokens must migrate by January 1, 2027. Not verified on a Shopify-owned page.
evidence.quote: public apps using non-expiring offline access tokens must migrate before January 1, 2027.

evidence.claim: Public app listing requires a privacy policy, support and listing content, a demo store link, screenshots, a feature media item, and app details; apps must pass the App Store requirements and a best-practices review.
evidence.quote: Include a privacy policy (required)

evidence.claim: Listing guidance: 3-6 desktop screenshots at 1600x900, a 2-3 minute feature video or image, a demo development store link, app name of 30 characters or fewer, and a 100-character introduction.
evidence.quote: Include 3-6 desktop screenshots, including at least one of your app's UI.

evidence.claim: Apps must perform OAuth immediately before any other install step, and must not use pop-ups for OAuth.
evidence.quote: Your app should immediately authorize using OAuth before any other steps occur

evidence.claim: Apps using APIs that will be deprecated within 90 days cannot be submitted to the App Store.
evidence.quote: apps using APIs that will be deprecated within 90 days can't be submitted.

evidence.claim: Provide a complete screencast of setup and functionality, clear test instructions, and valid test credentials when the app connects to a third-party platform.
evidence.quote: Provide clear instructions and a complete screencast showing your app's setup process and functionality.

evidence.claim: Shopify does not publish a fixed review turnaround for the App Store; third-party guides report about one to two weeks per cycle, with paused-and-resubmit loops adding more time.
evidence.quote: Shopify publishes no guaranteed timeline; developers commonly report one to two weeks per cycle.

evidence.claim: Third-party sources give a faster 3-5 business day first-response baseline, and a 7-14 business day range for others. Neither is an official Shopify figure.
evidence.quote: most new apps see a first response within 3–7 business days.

evidence.claim: Public distribution (installable on many stores) requires Shopify approval and an App Store listing; custom distribution (one store, or stores in one Plus organization, or development stores) does not require approval.
evidence.quote: Public distribution also requires registering for the Shopify App Store, which has a one-time fee.

evidence.claim: A developer forum thread says official documentation cites 5-10 business days for review, and developers reported waits from 10 days to about a month. Treat as anecdotal.
evidence.quote: Official documentation states 5-10 business days

evidence.claim: Review status moves through Draft, Submitted, Reviewed, and Published, with a Paused state when core requirements fail; developers have to fix and resubmit.
evidence.quote: with a Paused state when core requirements fail.
flags: cited URL was not retrieved during this research run

evidence.claim: Shopify's Partner Dashboard offers a self-assessment review requirements checklist under the app's Distribution settings (API scopes, GDPR webhooks, billing, design, listing completeness).
evidence.quote: Find it under Apps > [Your App] > Distribution > App Store > Review requirements in your Partner dashboard.

evidence.claim: Three mandatory compliance webhooks must be implemented even for unlisted apps before approval.
evidence.quote: Even if you're building an unlisted app, you still need to implement them.

evidence.claim: Unlisted public apps still go through the public app review. Shopify community participants say an unlisted app is hidden from search but still reviewed, and that the custom distribution method is the route if no review is wanted (but limited to one store or one Plus organization).
evidence.quote: If you don't want to go through the Public app review, you would need to setup your app with the Custom distribution method

evidence.claim: Unlisted apps (limited visibility) are not searchable or crawled in the App Store but can still be installed through their listing URL; the community treats this as the same review path.
evidence.quote: Is "Unlisted public" app type still supported?

evidence.claim: Development stores work without approval, so you can build and test with a public app before review; Shopify reviews public apps before they install on production stores.
evidence.quote: Shopify reviews all public apps before they can be installed on production stores (development stores work without approval).

evidence.claim: Dev Dashboard path for custom apps: create the app, provide name, URL and redirection URLs, click Generate link, then enter a myshopify.com domain to get an installation link.
evidence.quote: To authenticate with Shopify by using a custom app, you need to generate an installation link from your Partner Dashboard.

evidence.claim: Existing legacy custom apps keep working and are not affected by the January 2026 change, but new admin-created custom apps cannot be made.
evidence.quote: Existing custom apps aren’t affected and will continue to work.

evidence.claim: The distribution method cannot be changed once selected, and it should be chosen on the production app if separate dev and prod apps exist.
evidence.quote: You can't change the distribution method after you select it.

evidence.claim: Shopify's standard OAuth flow: a developer's app is told to escape iframes before redirecting for embedded apps, and the grant screen is shown in the merchant's admin.
evidence.quote: you can't perform a redirect from inside an iframe in the Shopify admin

evidence.claim: Apps must not require a separate sign-up before OAuth is the first step; some reviewers have flagged install flows that begin at the app's own login page.
evidence.quote: During an automated check, your app didn't successfully initiate authentication when installing.

evidence.claim: Custom distribution is limited to a single store, stores in one Plus organization, or development stores, and cannot charge through Shopify's app billing system.
evidence.quote: Can't charge merchants through Shopify's app billing system

evidence.claim: Legacy 'unpublished' public apps were deprecated in December 2019 and no longer need no-approval install; the Shopify Admin custom-app route for new apps closed on January 1, 2026.
evidence.quote: Unpublished apps: Deprecated as of December 9, 2019.

evidence.claim: Shopify states that custom apps can no longer be created from the Shopify admin starting January 1, 2026; new custom apps should be built in the Dev Dashboard and installed on the store. Existing custom apps keep working.
evidence.quote: To create a new custom app after this date, use the Dev Dashboard to build the app, then install it on your store.

evidence.claim: Protected customer data is off by default; apps can declare the relevant scopes before approval, but the API does not return data from non-development stores until the app is approved for it.
evidence.quote: You can add the relevant scopes to your app, but the API won't return data from non-development stores until your app is configured and approved for protected customer data use.

evidence.claim: Requesting protected customer data for a public app is done in the Partner Dashboard: open Apps, select the app, go to API access requests, click Request access for Protected customer data, give reasons, add name/address/email/phone fields individually with reasons, complete Data protection details, then submit for review.
evidence.quote: Complete your Data protection details, making sure that your app meets the protected customer data requirements.

open_questions: PKCE: no Shopify page checked mentions PKCE, so it is unknown whether the authorization code grant accepts or requires it.
Install caps: no official limit was found for unreviewed or unlisted public apps. Community reports only describe installs during testing.

Offline token lifetime: the 60-minute expiry and refresh-token behaviour are reported only by a third-party blog. The official offline-access-tokens page could not be checked. Verify on shopify.dev before relying on it.
Exact Partner Dashboard steps for adding allowed redirection URLs and the version-based Dev Dashboard redirect config were not verified on an official page.
Unlisted public apps: official docs say public distribution needs approval, but community sources disagree on whether 'unlisted' skips review. Confirm on the Partner Dashboard distribution screen.
Review turnaround: no official figure. Community sources range from 3-5 business days to 1-2 weeks, with anecdotes up to about a month.
Invalid client ID handling: the authorize endpoint probe used a placeholder store and did not show how Shopify rejects unknown client IDs. A real development store is needed to test.
Composio's default redirect and authorize URLs are templates. The actual callback URI must be copied from your Composio auth config.
The Partner Dashboard itself and the app-store submission page were not checked directly. Field labels in this guide come from third-party or older sources and should be confirmed on screen.
Whether a data protection review applies depends on install volume and customer records. Shopify does not give a threshold.
